summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for cellulitis of the left lower extremity, presenting with sudden-onset swelling, erythema, and pain, likely originating from a minor foot injury after toenail trimming. He was treated with intravenous vancomycin and Zosyn due to inadequate response to initial oral therapy. Imaging ruled out DVT, abscess, and osteomyelitis. Blood cultures were negative, and urine culture showed asymptomatic Klebsiella colonization. His infection improved significantly over 11 days, and he was discharged on a 6-day course of oral Bactrim and Augmentin. His chronic conditions, including diastolic heart failure, diabetes, mechanical aortic valve on anticoagulation, and COPD, remained stable. Warfarin was adjusted to 5 mg daily with an INR of 2.5 at discharge. He was instructed to follow up with his PCP and continue all home medications.
